_README: The comparison against the live portal. You must fill this in by hand.
Nothing here may be estimated, inferred, or filled in by a model. A fabricated
benchmark discredits every other honest thing on the site. Every row stays
null until a human has actually observed it, and /evidence renders unfilled
rows as 'not yet counted' rather than hiding them.
How to fill it:
1. Open cybercrime.gov.in on a phone. Start a 'Financial Fraud' report.
2. Count every field that must be filled before the FIRST submission that
could reach a bank. Count an OTP screen as a step, not a field.
3. Time the same task end to end. Do it three times, record the median.
4. Set verified to true and fill measuredBy / measuredOn.
If you cannot get through the portal to count, leave it null and say so on
the page. 'We could not measure this' is a fine thing to show a judge.
'We guessed' is not.
STATUS: not counted, and not guessed. A documentary route was tried first --
the portal publishes citizen manuals at cybercrime.gov.in/Webform/Citizen_Manual.aspx,
but the financial-fraud one covers the 1930 helpline route (and is marked Delhi
only), and the general reporting manual is a scanned deck of screenshots with no
text layer and no field enumeration. Counting fields off screenshots of a form
that is not the financial-fraud form would be inference, which this file forbids.
So the portal column stays null until someone opens the live portal and counts.
